summary: This survey lists and describes general-purpose polyhedral compilers as of 2024 and compares eight of them on PolyBench/C for correctness and performance. Its measured targets are one shared-memory CPU node and one GPU, so it gives no treatment of distributed-memory targets, message passing, data placement or communication generation.
why_read: A newcomer gets a current list of general-purpose polyhedral compilers and a reproducible single-node benchmark of how they behave, which is useful background for loop-optimization work.
main_contribution: A catalog and classification of polyhedral compilers, with a robustness and performance comparison of eight tools on PolyBench/C.
main_limitation: The authors note that PolyBench/C is outdated, lacks machine-learning affine patterns and uses dataset sizes too small for current HPC nodes.
evaluation_method: benchmarking on PolyBench/C with perf counters, on one CPU node and one GPU
